bib.title: CoAT: Chain-of-Associated-Thoughts Framework for Enhancing Large Language Models Reasoning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "CoAT: Chain-of-Associated-Thoughts Framework for Enhancing Large Language Models Reasoning", Jianfeng Pan, Senyou Deng, Shaomang Huang (360 Security Technology), Findings of EMNLP 2025 (arXiv 2502.02390v3, 13 Nov 2025).

COVERAGE: 61440 of 61440 chars read (all pages, appendices included; references skimmed). Figures 1-10 are image-only, so only their captions were read. I did not run the figures script.

FIT WARNING FOR THE TARGET NOTE: CoAT is MCTS search over reasoning steps, with per-node "associative memory" (retrieved or self-generated extra facts). It is not about plan-writing with tools named, restating state, plans as DAGs, or choosing among many tools. The only loose links are these:
- The associative-memory step is a form of restating or augmenting state at each node.
- The External Brain is a tool or retriever choice, but it is KAG retrieval output in the experiments.
- The paper never tests tool naming, DAG plans or tool selection.
Likely use is a "sharpens"-style citation on search over plans or retrieval during reasoning, not support for the four sections.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Adding per-node associative memory lifts CRB score by about 10% in the ablation.
  number: Qwen2.5-32B 0.67 (no AM) to 0.77 (AM, β=0.1); Qwen2.5-72B 0.71 to 0.80. The paper says the gain is "approximately 10%".
  setup: CRB (self-built, 205 questions), full CoAT (MCTS) with and without AM. Scoring is by judge rules, and the paper does not name the judge model.
  quote: "incorporating the whole AM mechanism led to an approximately 10% improvement in average score compared to the baseline without AM."
  where: Sec 4.3, Table 3, around chars 30000-31500
- claim: Weighting the associative-content score (β) has little effect. The component, not the weighting, drives the gain.
  number: β=0 gives 0.75 (32B) and 0.77 (72B); β=0.1 gives 0.77 and 0.80.
  setup: CRB; β swept over [0,0.6] (Fig 8).
  quote: "although the value of β has little impact on the final score, the optimal result is achieved within the entire range whenβ= 0.1."
  where: Sec 4.3
- claim: CoAT beats KAG on three multi-hop QA sets with the same Qwen2.5-32B backbone.
  number: EM gains of 13.0, 7.2 and 13.4 points on HotpotQA, 2Wiki and MuSiQue. F1 gains are 2.1, 3.3 and 8.4. Table 1 EM: CoAT 69.6/73.1/34.7 vs KAG-Qwen 56.6/65.9/21.3.
  setup: 1,000-question subset of each validation set. CoAT's associative memory is KAG's retrieval output, so the retriever is shared. Baseline numbers other than KAG-Qwen are copied from the KAG documentation, with different backbones (ChatGPT-3.5, DeepSeek-V2 236B). CoAT does not win everywhere: KAG with DeepSeek-V2 beats it on MuSiQue EM (36.7 vs 34.7) and on MuSiQue and HotpotQA F1 (the F1 table cell is garbled in extraction).
  quote: "with EM gains of 13.0%, 7.2%, and 13.4% on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue respectively, and F1 improvements of 2.1%, 3.3%, and 8.4%."
  where: Sec 4.2, Table 1, around chars 15000-18000. The "%" signs are really percentage points.
- claim: On CRB, CoAT on open Qwen models outscores o1 and DeepSeek-R1.
  number: CoAT-32B 0.77, CoAT-72B 0.80; DeepSeek-R1 0.75; o1 0.73; base Qwen2.5-32B 0.55 and 72B 0.62. The paper reports relative gains of 22% and 18%.
  setup: CRB, 205 questions, rubric-scored. This is a single run with no variance reported. Baselines are single-pass, and the other models cost far less per question than a tree search. The comparison is not call-matched or compute-matched. The abstract says "more than 15% gain on our proprietary CRB dataset", while the body says 22% and 18% relative.
  quote: "relative gains of 22% and 18% in the evaluated scores, respectively."
  where: Sec 4.2, Table 2
  Arithmetic check: 0.77/0.55 = 1.40 and 0.80/0.62 = 1.29. The stated 22% and 18% gains do not match these ratios. They are closer to the 0.67-to-0.77 and 0.71-to-0.80 steps, which are 15% and 13%. Treat the quoted figures as unreliable and flag it.
- claim: CoAT raises the pairwise win rate by 50% (relative).
  number: 50%
  quote: "the Qwen series achieves a 50% relative improvement in the average win rate when using CoAT"
  setup: pairwise comparison of answers on "comprehensiveness and depth of detail" (Fig 6). The judge is not named in the text. Exact win rates sit in a heatmap image.
  where: Sec 4.2
- claim: The paper's search design, stated as settings.
  number: UCT exploration weight w=1.0, β=0.1, K candidate nodes (3 in the Fig 3 example), max depth D (D=-1 means no limit).
  quote: "w is the exploration weight and is set to 1.0 during CoAT reasoning." / "β is a weighting coefficient ... and is set to 0.1 in subsequent experiments."
  where: Sec 3.2

BASELINES: Neither call-matched nor compute-matched. No token, call or latency counts appear anywhere. The only cost statement is the limitation quoted below. The base models and the reasoning models are single-pass. There is no self-consistency, best-of-N or plain-RAG comparison at equal calls, so gains cannot be separated from extra compute. The ablation does hold the tree search fixed (w/o AM vs w/ AM), so it is the cleaner evidence for the AM component, though search cost per condition is not reported.

LIMITS
- Authors concede: "such improvement comes at the cost of increased reasoning time." They also say the CRB dataset still needs quality refinement.
- Not shown:
  - any cost or latency figure;
  - variance, seeds or significance;
  - judge model identity and judge bias;
  - tool use, agents, plan structure, tool selection;
  - the External Brain beyond KAG retrieval (no web search or agent EB results).
- The F1 drop is acknowledged: association makes the model add explanatory text when no direct answer exists, which lowers F1 ("which can reduce response precision and conse-quently lower the overall F1 score").
- DeepSeek-V2 numbers are copied from KAG docs; the authors swapped in Qwen2.5-32B because the API was shut down.
- The Fig 5 qualitative case is a single hand-picked question.
- The CRB dataset is built by the authors and mixes English and Chinese. It is released at github.com/IceSwordLab/CoAT.
- Dated: the comparison set is o1, o3-mini, R1, GPT-4o, Qwen2.5 (early 2025). Search-R1 is mentioned as conceptually aligned but costlier because it trains with RL.

BUILDS ON: MCTS/UCT (Kocsis and Szepesvári 2006; Coulom 2006); LATS (Zhou et al. 2023), which adds Evaluation and Reflection stages; RAP (Hao et al. 2023); LLM-MCTS (Zhao et al. 2024); Tree of Thoughts (Yao et al. 2024); Graph of Thoughts (Besta et al. 2024); CoT (Wei et al. 2022); CoT-SC (Wang et al. 2022); IRCoT (Trivedi et al. 2022a); KAG (Liang et al. 2024); HippoRAG (Gutiérrez et al. 2024); NativeRAG (Lewis et al. 2020); Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025); LangChain implementation.

CODE (verbatim, Sec 3 and Algorithm 1)
- Eq 1: AM(ni) = EB ↦ LLM(Q | G(ni))
- Eq 2: G(ni+1) = LLM(Q | G(ni) | AM(n1:i))
- Eq 3: UCT(n) = V(n) + w·sqrt(ln N(p) / N(n))
- Eq 4: V(n) = Fg(Q,G(n)) + β·Fa(G(n),AM(n))
- Algorithm 1 loop: "Selection: choose the best trajectory by UCT. / Generation (G*): ni ← LLM(Q|G|AM). / Association (AM*): ni ← LLM(Q|G*). / Evaluation (V): ni ← F(Q,G*) + βF(G*,AM*)." The Reward Model checks completion; the search stops at depth D.

FIGURES
- Fig 2 (Overview of CoAT, with an optional External Brain): the loop of expand, associate, evaluate.
- Fig 3 (detailed reasoning process, K=3, the AI-competition query): best for showing the loop on a worked example.
- Fig 4: the optimized MCTS cycle with the added Association stage.
- Fig 6 (win-rate heatmap) and Fig 7 (ablation win rates): numbers are only in the images.
- Fig 8: β sweep.
- Best candidate for a note: Fig 3, or Fig 4 as a small diagram of search with state augmentation.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- Table 1 extraction is partly garbled: the CoAT HotpotQA row reads "69.674.2", meaning EM 69.6 and F1 74.2 with bold lost. The F1 gains are taken from the paper's own text.
- Fig 6, 7, 8 and 10 values are not extractable.
- The abstract's ">10% on HotpotQA and MuSiQue" matches the EM gain of 13 points. The text's own EM claim for CoAT over KAG-DeepSeek ("7.1% and 5.3%") matches 69.6 vs 62.5 and 73.1 vs 67.8.
- Percentages in the paper are inconsistently absolute and relative (see the CRB arithmetic check above).
